slides.title: Function Decorators
slides.prompt: Decorators modify or extend the behavior of functions without changing their source code.

slides.title: Decorator Syntax Symbol
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol used to apply a decorator above a function definition.

slides.title: First-Class Functions
slides.prompt: What does it mean that functions are 'first-class citizens' in Python?
options: They can be passed as arguments, returned, and assigned to variables
They can only be defined at class scope
They are pre-compiled into C code
slides.correctAnswer: They can be passed as arguments, returned, and assigned to variables

slides.title: Lambda Functions
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to create an anonymous single-expression function.

slides.title: Map Function
slides.prompt: What does map(lambda x: x*2, [1, 2, 3]) do?
options: Applies the function to all items in the iterable
Reduces list to a single number
slides.correctAnswer: Applies the function to all items in the iterable

slides.title: Filter Function
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to extract elements that satisfy a condition.

slides.title: Functools Wraps
slides.prompt: Why is @functools.wraps(func) used inside custom decorators?
options: To preserve original function metadata (like __name__ and __doc__)
To prevent recursion depth limit errors
slides.correctAnswer: To preserve original function metadata (like __name__ and __doc__)
